title: Leonida & Vice City
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI returns to the fictional state of Leonida, a sun-bleached peninsula of causeways, wetlands, and neon coastline. Vice City is its loudest address: a modern resort metropolis built for money, music, and bad decisions. The revealed story follows Jason and Lucia through a state that treats every sunset like a premiere.

title: Vice City, 1986
summary: The 2002 classic turned the series into a period piece: pastel suits, synth-pop, oceanfront clubs, and a criminal economy with a taste for chrome. Tommy Vercetti arrives in a city that rewards confidence and punishes sentiment, and the game's radio dial becomes as memorable as its skyline.

title: San Andreas, 1992
summary: Three cities, one enormous state, and a homecoming story about family, loyalty, and territory. San Andreas mixes early-90s West Coast culture with a road-trip structure: Los Santos, San Fierro, and Las Venturas each bring a different rhythm, skyline, and kind of trouble.

title: Los Santos, 2013
summary: Grand Theft Auto V splits its story across three protagonists and one sprawling satirical metropolis. Michael, Franklin, and Trevor move between heists, hobbies, and the entertainment industry's endless appetite for reinvention. The result is a West Coast playground built around planning, improvisation, and spectacle.

title: Liberty City, 2008
summary: Grand Theft Auto IV trades sunshine for overcast steel. Niko Bellic arrives in Liberty City chasing an idea of success and finds a colder city of immigrants, debts, and old wars. The game's tone is grounded, its streets dense, and its story less about empire than about the cost of trying to leave one behind.

title: The Warriors, 1979
summary: Rockstar's brawler expands Walter Hill's cult film into a long, dangerous night across a stylized New York. Gangs own the subway map, turf is measured in blocks and platforms, and the journey home becomes the whole story. The game's look leans on graffiti, turnstiles, and fluorescent light.

title: The Frontier, 1899
summary: Red Dead Redemption 2 is a prequel about the end of an era: a gang trying to stay useful while the world builds fences and railroads around it. Snow, swamp, prairie, and city all share the same slow rhythm. The frontier here is less a place to conquer than a story people keep telling themselves.

title: Bullworth Academy, 2006
summary: Bully trades city blocks for school corridors, cliques, and small-town gossip. Jimmy Hopkins navigates a private academy where the hierarchy is absurdly serious and the calendar is a social weapon. It is a Rockstar game about territory at a much smaller scale, with the same eye for satire.

title: The franchise, from 1997
summary: Grand Theft Auto began as a top-down crime game from DMA Design and grew into one of the most recognizable open-world series in the medium. Each era added a new city, a new voice, and a new way to measure freedom: from arcade chaos to cinematic scale.

title: Rockstar Games
summary: Rockstar Games was established as a publishing label under Take-Two Interactive in 1998. Its studios have built a catalog across crime, westerns, noir, and schoolyard satire, with a house style that favors dense worlds, strong radio soundtracks, and sharply observed fiction.

title: Tommy Vercetti
summary: A made man with a long memory and a short temper. Tommy arrives in Vice City expecting a debt to be settled and decides to collect the whole city instead. His story is about refusing to be anyone's subordinate.

title: Carl 'CJ' Johnson
summary: A returning son who spends most of San Andreas trying to keep his family together while the city pulls it apart. CJ is loyal, practical, and increasingly aware that loyalty is not a plan.

title: Niko Bellic
summary: A war veteran chasing a ghost through Liberty City. Niko's story is about the difference between the life he was promised and the one he keeps choosing.

title: Michael, Franklin & Trevor
summary: Three protagonists with incompatible ideas about success. Michael wants meaning, Franklin wants distance from the block, and Trevor wants to be the only honest person in the room.

title: Jason & Lucia
summary: The revealed leads of GTA VI: a partnership built on trust in a state that rewards self-interest. Their story is framed as a modern crime romance rather than a lone-wolf rise.

title: Grove Street Families
summary: A neighbourhood outfit defined by history, loyalty, and a losing war for territory. Grove Street is less a gang than a memory of one, which is exactly what makes it worth fighting for.

title: The Lost MC
summary: A motorcycle club held together by tradition and torn apart by ego. The Lost are at their most dangerous when they are trying to prove they still matter.

title: The Vercetti Organisation
summary: A crew built out of borrowed loyalty and purchased property. By the end of 1986 it controls clubs, businesses, and the kind of silence that money can buy.

title: The gangs of 1979
summary: The Warriors turns the New York night into a patchwork of turf, colours, and grudges. Every bridge is a border and every train car is somebody's territory.

title: Bullworth's cliques
summary: Bullworth Academy is a small world with big politics: jocks, preppies, greasers, nerds, and everyone else trying to survive the timetable. The satire is sharp because the stakes feel real.
